candidates.title: Subliminal Learning in Vision-Language Models
candidates.content: Subliminal learning is a phenomenon in large language models (LLMs) where a teacher passes a hidden preference to a student through training data unrelated to that preference. We study whether subliminal learning also occurs in vision-language models (VLMs). We finetune a teacher VLM to prefer a specific animal or facial attribute and use a control teacher from the same base model. Both teachers generate numbers for an unrelated visual task involving geometric shapes. Two students initialized from the same base VLM are finetuned on the same images, using numbers generated by either the biased or control teacher. Across VLMs ranging from 2B to 7B parameters, we find that both animal and facial preferences can transfer through this unrelated task. Students trained on biased-teacher outputs select the target more often than control students, with a difference of up to sim10 percentage points in the animal preference task. Transfer can become stronger with more training data and varies with the target preference, model, and how the numbers are generated. Beyond preferences, we show that the biased student's explanations use more of the same words and phrases as the biased teacher's exp

candidates.title: Probing Transformer Representations Layer by Layer, Module by Module
candidates.content: Which representation should be probed in a transformer-based foundation model? Recent work shows that the standard practice of probing the final layer is often suboptimal, as intermediate layers can provide better features. Yet, representations are still largely studied along depth alone, treating each transformer block as an atomic unit. In this work, we analyze transformer representations layer by layer, module by module. Through more than 144,000 linear probing evaluations of vision foundation models (VFMs) and large language models (LLMs), we show that layer and module choices should be considered jointly: the best layer-module pair yields substantially larger gains over the final-layer residual stream than the best layer with the residual stream fixed. Moreover, module performance can vary substantially across layers, showing that useful representations cannot be characterized by depth alone. Building on these findings, we evaluate simple fixed probing strategies: the final-layer feedforward activation (Act@100) for vision and the second normalization layer at 60% depth (LN2@60) for language. These strategies improve over the probing baseline in a majority of evaluations and r

candidates.title: CARTBench: Rubric-Based Evaluation of Shopping Advice for Complex and Ambiguous Requests with Timelines
candidates.content: Large language model (LLM) shopping assistants now recommend products in multi-turn conversations. However, reliable evaluation faces Data scarcity and Difficulty Standardizing Criteria. To address these obstacles, we introduce CARTBench for CART (Complex and Ambiguous Requests with Timelines). For Data scarcity, we curate cases from real commercial shopping needs across 17 retail domains, pairing timestamped dialogue with 1,603 product records. For Difficulty Standardizing Criteria, we develop case-specific rubrics guided by Ideal Response Principles, distilled from excellent replies manually selected from successfully completed orders. These principles also guide Principle-Guided CART Prompting, our structured recommendation strategy. The experimental benchmark contains 1,328 expert-annotated criteria across Core, Excellence, and Safety. To answer the CART question, we evaluate 7 flagship commercial API models, including GPT-6.1-Sol and Claude-Opus-5, and 35B+ parameters open-weight models. candidates.title: llm-gemini 0.37
candidates.content: Release: llm-gemini 0.37 Google launched Gemini 4 Hydrogen today - the lowest cost member of the Gemini 4 family. It's actually not too far off the price of its much bigger siblings, Carbon and Argon. I'm finding Gemini 4's pricing really confusing. Here's the pricing scheme: Model Dates Input ($/M) Cached input Output Gemini 4 Carbon Through Nov 30, 2026 $2.00 $0.10 $10.00 From Dec 1, 2026 $4.00 $0.20 $20.00 Gemini 4 Argon Through Nov 30, 2026 $2.00 $0.10 $10.00 From Dec 1, 2026 $4.00 $0.20 $20.00 Gemini 4 Hydrogen $1.50 $0.075 $7.50 Carbon and Argon are the same price , and both are scheduled to double in price on December 1st. If they're the same price, why have two different models? Google says that Argon "delivers Gemini 4 intelligence with faster responses and lower token spend per turn compared to Gemini 4 Carbon" - so it may be priced the same, but it will use less tokens per task. Hydrogen, supposedly the cheap model, is currently only a 25% discount on its more capable peers. The Hydrogen price will make more sense after December 1st, when it will represent a 75% discount. It's still considerably more expensive than Claude Haiku 5.5 and GPT-6 Luna - they're both $0.10/$0.

candidates.content: Release: llm-anthropic 0.31 Anthropic released Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 today. Fable 5.2 is currently ranked first on Artificial Analysis . You can see them all here - here's the best result I got, from xhigh : max failed to return an image at all, running out of tokens after spending 128,000 thinking about them . That's the same bug that I saw with Opus 5.5 - but it's new for the Fable series, both Fable 5 and Fable 5.1 returned max effort pelicans just fine. This study evaluates the real-world effectiveness, safety, and immunogenicity of a single dose of the Vi-CRM197 typhoid conjugate vaccine (TCV) delivered through a mass vaccination campaign in selected districts of Madagascar. The study targets individuals aged 9 months to 45 years living in defined catchment areas with a high burden of typhoid fever. Additional outcomes include clinically suspected typhoid fever, severe disease, vaccine safety, immunogenicity, antibiotic use and consumption, and carriage of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) markers. Malaria caused by Plasmodium falciparum continues to be a global problem with devastating consequences. A greater understanding of the immunologic and parasitologic factors associated with infection and disease is badly needed; and will accelerate the development of highly protective vaccines for both mothers and children. Pregnancy malaria is associated with low birth weight, maternal anemia, and gestational hypertension, and both inflammation and the fetal response to infection may contribute to these poor outcomes. Childhood malaria is a major cause of mortality, and we have found that its risk is related to in utero exposure to pregnancy malaria, as well as other host factors like iron status and constitutive cytokine levels. Pregnancy malaria is caused by a distinct parasite binding phenotype, and as our primary hypothesis in this study we speculate that severe childhood malaria parasites may also have distinct features. candidates.title: A p32 family RNA editing factor acts in mitochondrial ribosome biogenesis
candidates.content: Abstract Biogenesis of mitochondrial ribosomes (mitoribosomes) in the unicellular parasite Trypanosoma brucei requires an exceptionally large toolkit of assembly factors, identified in stable precursors of large and small mitoribosomal subunits (mtLSU and mtSSU) by cryoEM. Here, using genetic modifications and proteomic characterization of the immunoprecipitated assemblosome, the earliest characterized mtSSU precursor, we determined that a cap of its distinctive protrusion of hitherto unknown composition consists of a p22 homotrimer. This protein was previously implicated in the uridine-insertion editing of the cytochrome c oxidase subunit II transcript. Our functional analysis confirmed this role but revealed that its ablation also causes a loss of mtSSU and a systemic reduction in mitochondrial translation, phenocopying the depletion of established mitoribosomal assembly factors. Consequently, the oxidative phosphorylation system and mitochondrial function are compromised. The p22 protein belongs to the p32 family. candidates.title: Bipartite DNA-binding domain of transcription factor BCL11B binds clustered short DNA sequence motifs
candidates.content: Abstract B-cell leukemia/lymphoma 11B (BCL11B), despite its name, is a key regulator of T-cell development, lineage specification, and T-cell malignancies. BCL11B contains a bipartite DNA-binding domain composed of two C2H2 zinc finger arrays: low-affinity ZF2-3 and high-affinity ZF4-6. These arrays recognize similar six-nucleotide motifs, TG( n )CC( n ), as seven of the eight DNA base-contacting residues are conserved between them. The most conserved interactions involve the central GG dinucleotides, recognized by arginine and lysine residues at the key base-interacting positions of ZF3 and ZF5. We determined eight crystal structures of ZF2-3 bound to 12- or 20-base pair DNA duplexes containing either one or two binding motifs. The structures reveal that ZF2-3 recognizes DNA with remarkable configurational flexibility, binding motifs on either the same or opposite DNA strands with variable spacing in three relative orientations: head-to-tail (or tail-to-head), head-to-head, and tail-to-tail. candidates.title: Strand-displacement amplification reduces structure-induced PCR bias and preserves structurally diverse aptamers during SELEX
candidates.content: Abstract Stable secondary structures are important for aptamer folding and target recognition, but they can introduce structure-dependent amplification bias during Systematic Evolution of Ligands by Exponential Enrichment (SELEX), with G-quadruplexes (G4s) representing the most demanding case. Here, we introduce strand-displacement SELEX (SD-SELEX), which employs a polymerase with robust 5′→3′ strand-displacement activity to improve the amplification of structured templates. Comparative analyses showed that SD polymerase efficiently amplified hairpin- and G4-forming templates, whereas Taq polymerase exhibited structure-dependent amplification variability. In parallel thrombin SELEX experiments, SD-SELEX achieved 37-fold greater structural preservation and 65-fold higher batch-to-batch reproducibility than Taq-SELEX over 11 rounds. High-throughput sequencing further showed that SD-SELEX maintained G4 motif representation and progressively enriched the known 15-mer thrombin-binding aptamer through round 8, after which it was gradually replaced by newly identified G4 variants, whereas Taq-SELEX progressively depleted these sequences. candidates.title: Coupling environmental biosensors to inverter circuits in soil bacteria
candidates.content: Genetic logic gates, such as inverting NOT functions, are routinely designed and optimised for a narrow set of laboratory-standard chemical inputs. This reliance limits their utility in real-world applications, where engineered chassis must navigate complex, niche-specific signals. Focusing on environmental synthetic biology, we engineered four biosensors responsive to ecologically relevant physical and chemical inputs (iron, oxygen, temperature, and light) and systematically coupled them to three repressor-based NOT logic gates (QacR, SrpR, and LitR) to generate 12 composite sensor-gate circuits. To evaluate cross-host robustness, all constructs were benchmarked in two non-model soil bacteria: Pseudomonas putida KT2440 and Pseudomonas protegens Pf-5. Our findings demonstrate that overall circuit performance is non-additive and cannot be predicted simply by summing individual sensor and gate dynamics. While standalone biosensors reliably detected their cognate inputs, concatenation across regulatory junctions introduced non-linearities, emergent dynamics, and host-dependent effects that caused several pairings to deviate unexpectedly from their predicted behaviour. candidates.title: Sense-to-sense changes in bacterial genetic codes: Experimental validation by cell-free translation and native-host proteomics
candidates.content: In the sixty years since the publication of the complete genetic code [1], many variants of the classical codon table [2] have been observed to occur naturally, including both stop codon and sense-to-sense reassignment, but in bacteria the only experimentally validated variants are stop-codon reassignments. Recently, computational analysis with Codetta predicted bacterial genetic codes containing sense-to-sense changes. Using an Escherichia coli cell-free protein synthesis (CFPS) system, we tested tRNAs predicted to reassign arginine codons to tryptophan. These candidate CGG-decoding tRNAs from bacteria phylogenetically distant from E. coli restored cyan fluorescence from an sfGFP Y66R reporter in a dose-dependent manner when added to CFPS extracts containing canonical tRNAArg(CCG). Reactions lacking the CGG-to-Trp candidate tRNA remained near background. Reassignment was also observed with firefly luciferase and NanoLuc reporters, in which Trp incorporation restored activity and solubility. candidates.title: [Correspondence] Evidence and gaps for preventing postpartum haemorrhage – Authors’ reply
candidates.content: We thank Judith Lieber and colleagues and Gabriele Saccone and colleagues for their responses to our Series. Lieber and colleagues’ comment highlights the importance of distinguishing evidence for prevention from evidence for treatment. We agree with them that tranexamic acid is a life-saving treatment for postpartum haemorrhage and should be given promptly after diagnosis. The WOMAN trial showed that early tranexamic acid use for the treatment of postpartum haemorrhage is useful.1 This evidence for treatment, however, should not be interpreted as evidence for prevention, nor be used as the basis for recommending universal prophylaxis in high-burden countries.

candidates.title: SmartTrade acquires Celoxica
candidates.content: SmartTrade Technologies SAS (smartTrade), a global leader in multi-asset electronic trading and payments solutions, today announced that it has acquired Celoxica, a specialist provider of ultra-low latency execution infrastructure for listed Equities, Futures, Fixed Income, and Options. Celoxica is now part of the smartTrade Group.

candidates.title: AviaGames partners Visa for player payouts
candidates.content: AviaGames, a leader in casual, skill-based mobile games, is collaborating with Visa, a world leader in digital payments, and Global Payments®, a leading payment technology and software company, to give eligible U.S. players the ability to receive payouts from Avia’s mobile games directly to their eligible Visa cards.

candidates.title: Uber adds Revolut Pay option
candidates.content: Revolut, the global bank with over 80 million customers and 850,000 business clients, today announced a milestone payments partnership expansion with Uber, the world’s leading ride-hailing and delivery platform operating in 75 countries and serving over 215 million monthly active platform consumers across the world.

candidates.title: DTCC tokenisation service to connect with Solana
candidates.content: The Depository Trust & Clearing Corporation (DTCC), the premier post-trade market infrastructure for the global financial services industry, today announced plans to enable the tokenization of eligible The Depository Trust Company (DTC)-custodied assets on Solana.

candidates.title: Payment Options picks Tribe to power acquiring across Apac and Cema
candidates.content: Payment Options, a Singapore-headquartered Payment Service Provider, has partnered with Tribe Payments, a global issuer and acquirer processor, to provide payment processing technology and connectivity for its Acquiring business.

candidates.title: Wolters Kluwer streamlines lending for community banks and credit unions
candidates.content: Wolters Kluwer Financial & Corporate Compliance today announced the launch of ComplianceOne Plus, a cloud-based platform designed specifically for commercial and consumer lending at community banks and credit unions.

candidates.title: Nebius tests the neocloud playbook with $40 billion in planned spending
candidates.content: Nebius plans to fund its $40 billion AI infrastructure expansion through customer prepayments and loans, even as delays at a Microsoft data center raise questions about its financing model.

candidates.title: Merchants sue feds over Illinois card fee law
candidates.content: Trade groups filed lawsuits against bank and credit union regulators over a preemption of a state law that bans swipe fees for taxes and tips.

candidates.title: Uber’s UK banking partner Griffin raises $20M for stablecoin services
candidates.content: The Series B valued Griffin at more than $100 million and will help fund stablecoin reserve services and onchain cross-border payments.

candidates.title: Fiserv preps debit network sale
candidates.content: The processing giant is shifting customers to one of its debit networks in anticipation of selling or shuttering a second one, the company’s CEO said Tuesday.
